questions.q: The maximum vertical height to which a man can throw a ball is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>136</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The maximum horizontal distance upto which he can throw the same ball is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum height is achieved when the projection is along the vertical direction,

Hmax=v22 g=136 m

Now, for maximum range, angle of projection should be 45°. Therefore,

Rmax=v2 g=2Hmax

=2136

=272 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
mω2acosθ=mgsinθ

ω=gtanθa

y=4cx2

tanθ=dydx=8xC

questions.q: A bomb is dropped by a fighter plane flying horizontally. To an observer sitting in the plane, the trajectory of the bomb is a :
options: straight line vertically down the plane
parabola in a direction opposite to the motion of plane
parabola in the direction of motion of plane
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The bomb after being dropped from the plane will have only horizontal velocity but zero vertical velocity. This scenario is as same as if a body is horizontally projected from the top of a tower, and it hits the ground tracing a parabolic path. Hence, the trajectory of the bomb is also a parabola, in the direction of motion of the plane. But if we look the trajectory with respect to observer sitting in the plane then this looks like straight line vertically down the plane due to same horizontal velocity.

questions.q: The distance of the Sun from earth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and its angular diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2000</mn><mo>''</mo></math> when observed from the earth. The diameter of the Sun will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Diameter of Sun is D=rθ

=1.5×1011×(2000)×13600×π180=1.45×109 m

questions.q: Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of \(\left(45^{\circ}-\alpha\right)\) and \(\left(45^{\circ}+\alpha\right)\), respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Max}}=\frac{(\mathrm{u} \sin \theta)^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \frac{\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_1}{\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_2}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2(45-\alpha)}{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2(45+\alpha)} \\ & =\frac{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha\right)^2}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha\right)^2} \\ & =\frac{1-\sin 2 \alpha}{1+\sin 2 \alpha}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A child of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is going round a merry-go-round that makes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> rotation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The radius of the merry-go-round is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The centrifugal force on the child will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The angular speed ω of the child can be calculated as follows:

ω=2π3.14=2 rad s-1

The formula to calculate the centrifugal force on the child is given by

Fr=mω2r   ...(1)

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required centrifugal force.

Fr=5 kg×2 rad s-12×2 m=40 N

questions.q: A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a distance <math><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> from it. If <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the product <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know for complementary angle range is same for same projection speed.
t1=2usin(θ)g ….. (i)
t2=2usin(90-θ)g ….. (ii)
R=2u2sinθcosθg .… (iii)
From equation (i) and (ii)
t1t2=4 U2sinθ cosθg2
(Using the value of R from equation iii)
t1t2=2Rg

questions.q: A particle is moving with constant speed in a circular path. When the particle turns by an angle 90°, the ratio of instantaneous velocity to its average velocity is π:x2. The value of x will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In circular motion with constant speed, magnitude of instantaneous velocity, vins=ωr.

Time taken to turn by 90° will be =π2ω=π2ω.

Displacement will be equal to the length of AB=r2+r2=r2

Average velocity

vavg=displacementtime=r2×2ωπ=22πωr

Hence, required ratio vins vavg =ωrπ22ωr=π22

Therefore, x=2.

questions.q: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & 4 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\sin ^2 \theta \\ & 4=\tan \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A disc is rolling without slipping on a surface. The radius of the disc is R. At t=0, the top most point on the disc is A as shown in figure. When the disc completes half of its rotation, the displacement of point A from its initial position is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The displacement is the hypotenuse of the diameter and the distance travelled for half the rotation πR.

By using Pythagoras theorem,

Displacement of A=(2R)2+(πR)2

=Rπ2+4

questions.q: A projectile is launched at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> with the horizontal with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. After <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, its inclination with horizontal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>tan</mi><mi>β</mi></math> will be : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Component of velocity in horizontal direction,

vx=20cosα=v2cosβ

Component of velocity in vertical direction,

vy=20sinα-g×10=v2sinβ

⇒tanβ=20sinα-10020cosα

⇒tanβ=tanα-5cosα

⇒tanβ=tanα-5secα

questions.q: A player kicks a football with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> from the ground. What are the maximum height and the time taken by the football to reach at the highest point during motion? (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
θ=45°

H=u2sin2θ2g=(25)2×122×10=1258 m

and time t=T2

=usinθg=251210=25102=522s

questions.q:
A body of mass 10 kg is projected at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point 20,10. If T is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time t=T2, is _____ .
[Take g=10 m s-2]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that the projectile passes through 20,10 and angle of projection is θ=45°. Using the trajectory equation,

y=xtanθ-gx22u2cos2θ

⇒10=20-10100u2

⇒u=20 m s-1

Now the time of flight of projectile,

T=2usinθg

⇒T=220210=22 s⇒T2=2 s

Now velocity of the projectile at any time t can be written as,

v→=ucosθi^+usinθ-gtj^

⇒v→=102i^+(102-102]j^ m s-1

Therefore, momentum p→=Mv→=1002i^+1002-200j^ N s

From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is:

questions.solution:
A1A2=πRmax12πRmax22=u14u24=116

questions.q: Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, }\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_1=8 \times\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_1}{2 \mathrm{~g}}=8 \times \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_2}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \theta_1=2 \sqrt{2} \sin \theta_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_1 / \mathrm{g}}{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_2 / \mathrm{g}}=\frac{\sin \theta_1}{\sin \theta_2}=2 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body is projected at $t=0$ with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at $t=1$ s is $R$. Neglecting air resistance and taking acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, the value of $R$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=10 \cos 60^{\circ}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=10 \cos 30^{\circ}=5 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ After $\mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm{sec}$ Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=|(5 \sqrt{3}-10)| \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}=10-5 \sqrt{3}$ Centripetal, acceleration $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}^{2}+\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}}=\frac{25+100+75-100 \sqrt{3}}{10 \cos \theta}$ From figure (using (i)) $\tan \theta=\frac{10-5 \sqrt{3}}{5}=2-\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=15^{\circ}\mathrm{R}=\frac{100(2-\sqrt{3})}{10 \cos 15}=2.8 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: The initial speed of a projectile fired from ground is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math>. At the highest point during its motion, the speed of projectile is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>u</mi></math>. The time of flight of the projectile is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At maximum height, only horizontal velocity of the particle remains. Let the angle of project be θ. The horizontal velocity of the particle will remain same, therefore

ucosθ=3u2⇒θ=30°

Now, time of flight of projectile is

T=2usinθg=ug

questions.q: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> projected with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> making an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular momentum at maximum height will be, L=mucosθh, where h=maximum height

Therefore, L=mucosθ×u2sin2θ2g

=mu32g×32×122=3mu316g

questions.q: A projectile is projected with velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> with the horizontal. After <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> seconds its inclination with horizontal becomes zero. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> represents horizontal range of the projectile, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> will be : [use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>use</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the information given in the question, after time t the inclination of the projectile becomes zero i.e. the projectile is at the highest point. Therefore,

t=T2=usinθg.

The rang of the projectile R=2u2sinθcosθg.

Now,

Rt2=2u2sinθcosθg×g2u2sin2θ=2gcotθ⇒θ=cot-1R20t2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
y=2x-9x2
Comparing above equation with general equation of trajectory of projectile y=xtan⁡θ1-xR
tan θ=2
⇒sin θ=25 or cos θ=15
θ=sin-125 or θ=cos-115
And R = 2/9
R=v02sin⁡2θg=29

questions.q: Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the body was projected at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, with horizontal then sum of the maximum heights, attained by the two projectiles, is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For two projectiles with same speed to have the same horizontal range, angle of projection will be θ1+θ2=90°.

Therefore, θ2=90°-60°=30°.

Now, required sum of maximum heights will be,

Hmax1+Hmax2=u2sin2θ12g+u2sin2θ22g

=4022014+34=80 m

questions.q:
The projectile motion of a particle of mass 5 g is shown in the figure.

The initial velocity of the particle is 52 ms-1 and the air resistance is assumed to be negligible. The magnitude of the change in momentum between the points A and B is x×10-2 kgms-1. The value of x, to the nearest integer, is ___ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
|u→|=|v→|

u→=ucos45i^+usin45j^

v→=vcos45i^-vsin45j^

|ΔP→|=mv→-u→

ΔP=2musin45°=2×5×10-3×52×12

ΔP=50×10-3=5×10-2.

questions.q:
A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ from horizontal at a speed of $60 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $\mathrm{h}_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0: h_1$ is _________
[Take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{S}_1=30 \times 1-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 1=25 \\ & \mathrm{~S}_3=30+\left(\frac{-10}{2}\right) \times(2 \times 3-1)=5 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~S}_1}{\mathrm{~S}_3}=\frac{25}{5}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body starts falling freely from height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> hits an inclined plane in its path at height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math>. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>H</mi><mi>h</mi></mfrac></math> for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total time of flight =T can be written as, 

T=2hg+2H-hg

For maximum time =dTdh=0

⇒2g12h-12H-h=0

⇒H-h=h

⇒h=H2⇒Hh=2

questions.q: An object is projected in the air with initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math>. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____  degree.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum range is given by, Rmax=u2sin245°g=u2 g.

For the range to be half of the maximum range,

Rmax2=u22 g=u2sin2θg

⇒sin2θ=12

⇒2θ=30°or 2θ=150°

⇒θ=15°,75°

Therefore, answer is 15 or 75
